input.final_summary: Cursor does not provide a native setting/hook action to auto-open or focus the bottom Terminal panel when a new Agent chat starts. content.text:
1) **Direct support (auto open/focus terminal on new Agent session): `No`**

- I did not find any Cursor-native setting that says “on new Agent chat/session, open/focus bottom Terminal panel.”
- Cursor hooks do include `sessionStart`, but docs describe it as fire-and-forget and only document outputs for `env` and `additional_context` (not UI commands/panel focus): [Cursor Hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks.md).
- Agent/terminal docs describe terminal execution behavior and auto-run/sandbox settings, not UI panel auto-focus on session start: [Agent Terminal Tool](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/terminal.md), [Agent Overview](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview.md).

2) **Workaround options**

- **One-keystroke manual workflow (supported):** use a custom keybinding that runs multiple commands (`runCommands`) to start/open chat and toggle terminal.
  - Cursor points to VS Code keybinding system as baseline: [Cursor keyboard shortcuts reference](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md), [VS Code keybindings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/keybindings).
  - Command IDs documented by VS Code include:
    - `workbench.action.chat.newChat`
    - `workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal`
    - source: [Default keybindings reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/reference/default-keybindings).
- **Hook-triggered external automation (unsupported/brittle):**
  - Use `sessionStart` in `hooks.json` to run a script, then script calls OS automation (e.g., AutoHotkey/PowerShell UI automation) to bring Cursor window forward and send terminal shortcut.
  - This is not documented as a first-class Cursor UI API and can break with focus/timing/window-title changes.

3) **Exact mechanism/files (documented)**

- **Hooks config files** (where `sessionStart` is configured):
  - Project: `.cursor/hooks.json`
  - User: `~/.cursor/hooks.json`
  - Windows enterprise-level: `C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json`
  - source: [Cursor Hooks configuration](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks.md).
- **What `sessionStart` can do (documented):**
  - Input includes `session_id`, `is_background_agent`, `composer_mode`
  - Output supports `env` and `additional_context`
  - does **not** document “execute UI command” / “focus panel”
  - source: [Cursor Hooks: `sessionStart`](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks.md).
- **Keybindings mechanism** for workaround:
  - `keybindings.json` with `runCommands` (VS Code mechanism Cursor inherits)
  - source: [VS Code keybindings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/keybindings).

4) **Confidence + caveats**

- **Confidence:** **High** that there is no first-class Cursor setting/hook action for auto-focusing terminal specifically on new Agent session start.
- **Caveats:**
  - Cursor evolves quickly; a future release could add a dedicated setting/event action.
  - VS Code command-level workarounds are reliable for manual shortcuts, but still not “automatic on session-start event.”
  - Hook + OS automation is possible but inherently fragile and unofficial for this use case.
